HOW TO RUN THIS SCRIPT:

1. REQUIRED FILES AND FOLDER STRUCTURE:
   - This .Rmd file should be in your main working directory
   - Data file: "20250724_Final_data.xlsx" should be in the same folder as this .Rmd file
   - BibTeX file: "export.bib" should be in the same folder as this .Rmd file
   - Parser script: Create a folder called "Script" in the same directory, and place "bibtex_parser.R" inside it
   - Optional: "reference.docx" for custom Word formatting (if you have specific formatting requirements)

2. FOLDER STRUCTURE SHOULD LOOK LIKE:
   YourWorkingDirectory/
   ├── appendix.Rmd (this file)
   ├── 20250724_Final_data.xlsx (your data)
   ├── export.bib (your references)
   ├── reference.docx (optional formatting template)
   └── Script/
       └── bibtex_parser.R (BibTeX parsing script)

3. REQUIRED R PACKAGES:
   The script will automatically load these packages. If you don't have them installed, run:
   install.packages(c("flextable", "dplyr", "officer", "readxl", "stringr"))

4. HOW TO RUN:
   - Open this file in RStudio
   - Click the "Knit" button at the top of the editor
   - Or use Ctrl+Shift+K (Windows) / Cmd+Shift+K (Mac)
   - The output will be a Word document named "appendix.docx"

5. WHAT THE SCRIPT DOES:
   - Reads your Excel data file and filters for included studies
   - Creates a formatted table with study information
   - Matches studies to BibTeX references and creates a reference list
   - Exports everything to a Word document ready for publication

6. TROUBLESHOOTING:
   - If you get "file not found" errors, check that all files are in the correct locations
   - If references don't match properly, check that your BibTeX file contains the studies
   - If the table looks wrong, check that your Excel file has the expected column names

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# Load required packages
library(flextable)  # For creating formatted tables
library(dplyr)      # For data manipulation
library(officer)    # For Word document formatting
library(readxl)     # For reading Excel files
library(stringr)    # For text processing

# Source the BibTeX parser (if it exists)
bibtex_script_path <- file.path("Script", "bibtex_parser.R")
if (file.exists(bibtex_script_path)) {
  source(bibtex_script_path)
  
} else {
  
}
```

```{r data-preparation}
# Load and prepare the data
data <- read_excel("20250724_Final_data.xlsx")


# Filter for included studies and add Reference_ID
data_included <- data %>%
  filter(Inclusion_Exclusion == "Included") %>%
  mutate(
    # Clean the year formatting - handle both numeric years and "n.d."
    Publication_Year_Clean = case_when(
      grepl("n\\.d\\.|no date|nd", as.character(Publication_Year), ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "n.d.",
      TRUE ~ as.character(as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", as.character(Publication_Year))))
    ),
    # For sorting purposes, convert n.d. to a large number so it appears last
    Publication_Year_Sort = case_when(
      Publication_Year_Clean == "n.d." ~ 9999,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(Publication_Year_Clean)
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Publication_Year_Sort)) %>%
  mutate(Reference_ID = row_number()) %>%  # Add numbered references
  select(Reference_ID, everything())

# Merge scenario and population variables
data_included <- data_included %>%
  mutate(Corruption_Scenarios_Merged = apply(select(., starts_with("Corruption_Scenarios")), 1, function(x) {
    paste(na.omit(unique(x[x != ""])), collapse = ", ")
  })) %>%
  mutate(Target_Population_Merged = apply(select(., Public_Sector_Actors, Private_Sector_Actors, 
                                                 General_Public, Students, 
                                                 Demographic_Group, Target_Population_Other), 
                                          1, function(x) {
                                            paste(na.omit(unique(x[x != ""])), collapse = ", ")
                                          }))

# Create the appendix table with the existing Covidence ID
appendix_table <- data_included %>%
  select(
    Reference_ID,
    Covidence_ID,
    Authors,
    Publication_Year = Publication_Year_Clean,
    Region,
    Corruption_Scenarios_Merged,
    Settings_Class,
    Target_Population_Merged,
    Techniques_Class,
    Quality_Appraisal_Total_Score
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Year is already in character format to handle both numeric years and "n.d."
    Publication_Year = Publication_Year
  )

```

This appendix provides a comprehensive overview of all studies included in the systematic review.

## Table A1. List of Included Studies

```{r table-creation}
# Create flextable with improved formatting including Co Evidence ID
Table_A1 <- appendix_table %>%
  rename_with(~ gsub('_', ' ', .)) %>%
  flextable() %>%
  # Set specific column widths for better formatting (adjusted for new column)
  width(j = 1, width = 0.4) %>%  # Reference ID - narrow
  width(j = 2, width = 0.5) %>%  # Co Evidence ID - narrow
  width(j = 3, width = 1.6) %>%  # Authors - wide (reduced slightly)
  width(j = 4, width = 0.5) %>%  # Publication Year - narrow
  width(j = 5, width = 0.7) %>%  # Region - medium
  width(j = 6, width = 1.0) %>%  # Corruption Scenarios - wide (reduced slightly)
  width(j = 7, width = 0.7) %>%  # Settings Class - medium
  width(j = 8, width = 0.9) %>%  # Target Population - medium-wide
  width(j = 9, width = 0.7) %>%  # Techniques Class - medium
  width(j = 10, width = 0.5) %>%  # Quality Score - narrow
  # Font and size settings
  fontsize(size = 8, part = 'all') %>%  # Slightly smaller font to accommodate extra column
  font(fontname = 'Times New Roman', part = 'all') %>%
  # Alignment settings
  align(j = c(1, 2, 4, 10), align = 'center', part = 'all') %>%  # Center: ID, Co Evidence ID, Year, Score
  align(j = c(3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9), align = 'left', part = 'all') %>%  # Left: Authors, Region, etc.
  # Header formatting
  bold(part = 'header') %>%
  bg(bg = '#f0f0f0', part = 'header') %>%
  # Text wrapping
  valign(valign = 'top', part = 'all') %>%
  # Borders
  border_remove() %>%
  hline_top(border = fp_border(width = 2), part = 'header') %>%
  hline(i = 1, border = fp_border(width = 1), part = 'header') %>%
  hline_bottom(border = fp_border(width = 2), part = 'body') %>%
  # Padding
  padding(padding.top = 3, padding.bottom = 3, padding.left = 2, padding.right = 2, part = 'all') %>%  # Slightly tighter padding
  # Fix text wrapping for long content
  fix_border_issues()

Table_A1
```

## References

```{r references, results='asis'}
# Parse BibTeX file for proper references
bib_file <- "export.bib"

if (file.exists(bib_file) && exists("parse_bibtex_file")) {
  # Parse the BibTeX file
  bib_result <- tryCatch({
    parse_bibtex_file(bib_file)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Error parsing BibTeX file: ", e$message)
    NULL
  })
  
  if (!is.null(bib_result) && length(bib_result$formatted) > 0) {
    # Create references with improved matching
    
    for (i in 1:nrow(appendix_table)) {
      study_authors <- appendix_table$Authors[i]
      study_year <- appendix_table$Publication_Year[i]
      
      # Skip if authors or year is NA
      if (is.na(study_authors) || is.na(study_year)) {
        reference <- paste0(i, '. [Missing author or year information].')
        cat(reference, '\n\n')
        next
      }
      
      # Clean the year - handle both numeric years and "n.d."
      clean_year <- if(study_year == "n.d.") {
        "n.d."
      } else {
        as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", as.character(study_year)))
      }
      
      # Try multiple matching strategies
      ref_found <- FALSE
      matched_ref <- NULL
      
      # Strategy 1: Match by year and author
      for (j in 1:length(bib_result$formatted)) {
        bib_ref <- bib_result$formatted[j]
        
        if (is.na(bib_ref) || bib_ref == "") next
        
        # Check for year match (try different year formats in BibTeX formatted references)
        year_match <- if(clean_year == "n.d.") {
          # For n.d., look for common "no date" patterns
          grepl("n\\.d\\.|no date|nd\\b", bib_ref, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE)
        } else {
          year_patterns <- c(
            paste0("\\(", clean_year, "\\)"),      # (2024)
            paste0(" ", clean_year, "\\b"),        # space 2024
            paste0("^", clean_year, "\\b"),        # start with 2024
            paste0(clean_year, "\\.")              # 2024.
          )
          any(sapply(year_patterns, function(pattern) {
            grepl(pattern, bib_ref, perl = TRUE)
          }))
        }
        
        if (year_match) {
          # Extract and clean author names from study data
          # Handle different separator formats
          author_separators <- c(",", ";", "&", " and ")
          author_parts <- study_authors
          
          for (sep in author_separators) {
            if (grepl(sep, author_parts)) {
              author_parts <- unlist(str_split(author_parts, sep))
              break
            }
          }
          
          if (length(author_parts) == 1) {
            author_parts <- unlist(str_split(study_authors, " "))
          }
          
          author_parts <- str_trim(author_parts)
          
          # Try matching with different author formats
          for (author in author_parts[1:min(5, length(author_parts))]) {  # Check first 5 parts
            if (is.na(author) || author == "" || nchar(author) < 2) next
            
            # Extract potential last name
            author_clean <- str_trim(author)
            
            # Try different lastname extraction methods
            lastname_candidates <- c()
            
            # Method 1: If it looks like "LastName, FirstName"
            if (grepl(",", author_clean)) {
              lastname_candidates <- c(lastname_candidates, str_trim(str_split(author_clean, ",")[[1]][1]))
            }
            
            # Method 2: If it looks like "FirstName LastName"
            space_parts <- str_trim(unlist(str_split(author_clean, " ")))
            if (length(space_parts) > 1) {
              lastname_candidates <- c(lastname_candidates, space_parts[length(space_parts)])
            }
            
            # Method 3: Use the whole name if it's short and might be a lastname
            if (nchar(author_clean) >= 3 && nchar(author_clean) <= 15 && !grepl(" ", author_clean)) {
              lastname_candidates <- c(lastname_candidates, author_clean)
            }
            
            # Method 4: Check if any word in the author field matches
            author_words <- str_trim(unlist(str_split(author_clean, "[\\s,.-]+")))
            for (word in author_words) {
              if (nchar(word) >= 3) {
                lastname_candidates <- c(lastname_candidates, word)
              }
            }
            
            # Check if any lastname candidate matches the BibTeX reference
            for (lastname in unique(lastname_candidates)) {
              if (nchar(lastname) >= 3 && 
                  grepl(paste0("\\b", lastname, "\\b"), bib_ref, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE)) {
                matched_ref <- bib_ref
                ref_found <- TRUE
                break
              }
            }
            
            if (ref_found) break
          }
        }
        
        if (ref_found) break
      }
      
      # Strategy 2: If no match found, try just year matching with broader author matching
      if (!ref_found) {
        for (j in 1:length(bib_result$formatted)) {
          bib_ref <- bib_result$formatted[j]
          
          if (is.na(bib_ref) || bib_ref == "") next
          
          # Look for the year anywhere in the reference
          year_found <- if(clean_year == "n.d.") {
            grepl("n\\.d\\.|no date|nd\\b", bib_ref, ignore.case = TRUE)
          } else {
            grepl(as.character(clean_year), bib_ref)
          }
          
          if (year_found) {
            # Check if any substantial word from authors appears
            author_words <- str_trim(unlist(str_split(study_authors, "[^a-zA-Z]+")))
            author_words <- author_words[nchar(author_words) >= 4]  # Only words with 4+ characters
            
            for (word in author_words[1:min(10, length(author_words))]) {
              if (!is.na(word) && word != "" && 
                  grepl(paste0("\\b", word, "\\b"), bib_ref, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
                matched_ref <- bib_ref
                ref_found <- TRUE
                break
              }
            }
            
            if (ref_found) break
          }
        }
      }
      
      # Strategy 3: Very loose matching - just check if any significant author word appears anywhere
      if (!ref_found) {
        # Extract significant words from author string
        significant_words <- str_trim(unlist(str_split(study_authors, "[^a-zA-Z]+")))
        significant_words <- significant_words[nchar(significant_words) >= 5]  # 5+ character words
        
        if (length(significant_words) > 0) {
          for (j in 1:length(bib_result$formatted)) {
            bib_ref <- bib_result$formatted[j]
            
            if (is.na(bib_ref) || bib_ref == "") next
            
            for (word in significant_words[1:min(3, length(significant_words))]) {
              if (grepl(word, bib_ref, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
                # Double-check that the year is close (within 1 year) or is n.d.
                year_close_match <- if(clean_year == "n.d.") {
                  grepl("n\\.d\\.|no date|nd\\b", bib_ref, ignore.case = TRUE)
                } else {
                  grepl(as.character(clean_year), bib_ref) || 
                  grepl(as.character(clean_year - 1), bib_ref) ||
                  grepl(as.character(clean_year + 1), bib_ref)
                }
                
                if (year_close_match) {
                  matched_ref <- bib_ref
                  ref_found <- TRUE
                  break
                }
              }
            }
            
            if (ref_found) break
          }
        }
      }
      
      # Output the reference in Nature Human Behaviour format
      if (ref_found && !is.null(matched_ref)) {
        # Nature Human Behaviour format: Author(s). Title. Journal vol, pages (year).
        cat(paste0(i, '. ', matched_ref), '\n\n')
      } else {
        # Create basic reference in Nature Human Behaviour style if no match found
        year_display <- if(clean_year == "n.d.") "n.d." else paste0("(", clean_year, ")")
        basic_ref <- paste0(study_authors, '. [Title not available]. [Journal information not available] ', year_display, '. [Complete reference information not available in BibTeX file].')
        cat(paste0(i, '. ', basic_ref), '\n\n')
      }
    }
    
  } else {
    # Fallback to basic references if BibTeX parsing fails
    for (i in 1:nrow(appendix_table)) {
      authors <- ifelse(is.na(appendix_table$Authors[i]), "[Missing authors]", appendix_table$Authors[i])
      year <- ifelse(is.na(appendix_table$Publication_Year[i]), "[Missing year]", 
                     appendix_table$Publication_Year[i])  # Keep as-is since it can be "n.d." or numeric
      
      # Format in Nature Human Behaviour style
      year_display <- if(year == "n.d.") "n.d." else paste0("(", year, ")")
      reference <- paste0(i, '. ', authors, '. [Title not available]. [Journal information not available] ', year_display, '. [BibTeX file could not be parsed - please add complete reference information].')
      cat(reference, '\n\n')
    }
  }
  
} else {
  # Fallback if BibTeX file not found or parser not available
  for (i in 1:nrow(appendix_table)) {
    authors <- ifelse(is.na(appendix_table$Authors[i]), "[Missing authors]", appendix_table$Authors[i])
    year <- ifelse(is.na(appendix_table$Publication_Year[i]), "[Missing year]", 
                   appendix_table$Publication_Year[i])  # Keep as-is since it can be "n.d." or numeric
    
    # Format in Nature Human Behaviour style
    year_display <- if(year == "n.d.") "n.d." else paste0("(", year, ")")
    reference <- paste0(i, '. ', authors, '. [Title not available]. [Journal information not available] ', year_display, '. [BibTeX file not found or parser not available - please add complete reference information].')
    cat(reference, '\n\n')
  }
}
```
